\section[investir]{investir — to invest}

\label{lesson:PT-C392-investir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the instalment, then the Portuguese for the saving.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: investir}
\textbf{investir} — \textquotedblleft{}to invest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele investiu as poupanças numa casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He invested his savings in a house.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Investir em} — to invest in. Conjugated \emph{invisto, investes, investe}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{investir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{investīre} \textquotedblleft{}to clothe, to cover\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on \emph{vestis} \textquotedblleft{}garment\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short); the money sense came later.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{investir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{investir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{investir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the instalment, then the Portuguese for the saving, then say \emph{investir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does investir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To invest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o investimento]{o investimento — the investment}

\label{lesson:PT-C392-investimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the saving, then the Portuguese for to invest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o investimento}
\textbf{o investimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the investment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Comprar casa é um bom investimento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Buying a house is a good investment.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer um investimento} — to make an investment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{investimento} is built on \emph{investir} \textquotedblleft{}to invest\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-mento}; the verb comes from Latin \emph{investīre} \textquotedblleft{}to clothe, to cover\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on \emph{vestis} \textquotedblleft{}garment\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o investimento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o investimento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the saving, then the Portuguese for to invest, then say \emph{o investimento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[o juro]{o juro — the interest (on money)}

\label{lesson:PT-C392-juro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to invest, then the Portuguese for the investment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o juro}
\textbf{o juro} — \textquotedblleft{}the interest (on money)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O banco paga pouco juro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The bank pays little interest.}
\end{quote}

Mostly plural: \emph{os juros}; \emph{com juros} — with interest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{juro} comes from Latin \emph{iūre}, a form of \emph{iūs, iūris} \textquotedblleft{}right, law\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short): money due by right.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a taxa]{a taxa — the rate; the fee, the charge}

\label{lesson:PT-C392-taxa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the investment, then the Portuguese for the interest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a taxa}
\textbf{a taxa} — \textquotedblleft{}the rate; the fee, the charge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A taxa de juro subiu em janeiro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The interest rate went up in January.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Taxa} is also a fee: \emph{taxa de inscrição} — enrolment fee.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{taxa} is built on \emph{taxar} \textquotedblleft{}to tax, to set a price\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{taxāre} \textquotedblleft{}to touch sharply, to rate, to value\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a taxa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the investment, then the Portuguese for the interest, then say \emph{a taxa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[a inflação]{a inflação — the inflation}

\label{lesson:PT-C392-inflacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the interest, then the Portuguese for the rate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a inflação}
\textbf{a inflação} — \textquotedblleft{}the inflation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Com a inflação, tudo está mais caro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With inflation, everything is more expensive.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A taxa de inflação} — the inflation rate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inflação} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{īnflātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a blowing up, a swelling\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{īnflāre}, built on \emph{flāre} \textquotedblleft{}to blow\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): prices swell.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a inflação}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the interest, then the Portuguese for the rate, then say \emph{a inflação} again
